observations.attribute: location of cystic lesion and irregular mass
observations.value: In the left paracardiac area, a well-defined, relatively radiolucent (cystic-appearing) lesion is visible superior to a more opaque, irregular soft-tissue mass that extends from the mediastinum into the left paracardiac region.
Smooth, well-circumscribed margin consistent with a fluid-filled or air-filled structure (e.g., gastric fundus or herniated stomach).

The cystic lesion lies above the diaphragmatic contour and abuts the left heart border; the irregular mass appears contiguous with it and extends inferiorly toward the diaphragm but remains largely within the thorax near the left cardiophrenic angle.
Both lesions are confined to the left hemithorax, specifically the left paracardiac/mediastinal region.
No clear diaphragmatic defect visible; however, the positioning suggests herniation through the esophageal hiatus.

hypotheses.name: Mixed-type hiatal hernia (sliding + paraesophageal components)
hypotheses.basis: Coexistence of a smooth, cystic-appearing structure (likely gastric fundus in sliding component) superior to an irregular soft-tissue mass (herniated gastric body or omentum in paraesophageal component), both in left paracardiac region—classic for mixed-type hiatal hernia on CXR.

hypotheses.name: Gastric volvulus or intrathoracic stomach
hypotheses.basis: Irregular mass may represent twisted or distended stomach; cystic component could be gas-filled lumen. Requires correlation with clinical symptoms and possibly contrast study.

uncertainties: Exact nature of the cystic lesion (gas vs fluid vs mixed); cannot differentiate without fluoroscopy or CT.
